tools.list_group_candidates: List outputs that can be grouped with a given primary output. If none provided, uses first output of a named zone.
tools.group_outputs: Group outputs under a primary output. Bridge endpoint must support grouping.
tools.group_zones: Group outputs into a single zone (requires 2+ output_ids).
tools.ungroup_output: Ungroup a specific output from any group. Bridge endpoint must support ungrouping.
tools.transfer_playback: Transfer playback (and queue) to another zone. Tips: call list_zones just before this to ensure fresh zone IDs; iOS outputs (e.g., iPhone) may need the device unlocked/active to appear.
tools.tools_bridge_connection_status: Return the current RWAV Bridge connection status (connected/unavailable) and transport source (bonjour/ssdp/manual). Use this to confirm that the MCP has a reachable RWAV Bridge instance before issuing playback or queue operations.
tools.tools_help_open: Open RWAV Bridge MCP Help page
tools.tools_service_info_get: Get service-specific guidance and reliability notes for TIDAL/Qobuz. Use this to decide whether to prefer typed section readers (albums/playlists/tracks) or raw node_open navigation, and to understand known quirks before browsing or executing playback actions.
tools.tools_bridge_version_get: Return the installed RWAV Bridge version, plus the MCP server version. Use this to confirm that discovery and connection succeeded. Does not perform any browsing or playback operations.
tools.tools_bridge_set_base: Manually set the RWAV Bridge base URL or host. Use this when auto-discovery is blocked or misconfigured. Verify the new base via /capabilities; do not set repeatedly if verification fails. This affects all subsequent tool calls until cleared.
tools.tools_bridge_unset_base: Clear the manually set RWAV Bridge base URL. After unsetting, discovery will revert to bonjour/ssdp. Use when switching network environments or repairing misconfigurations.
tools.tools_playlist_discard: Discard a staged custom playlist plan
tools.tools_tracks_addnext_bulk: Bulk Add Next for ordered trackKeys (stable order, server-side). Use pause_for_addnext to control final state restoration for addnext (false restores pre-state; true allows paused; omitted preserves current behaviour). If pause_for_addnext is explicitly false, stable ordering is disabled to ensure non-disruptive playback (no internal pause).
tools.tools_genres_list: List Library/TIDAL/Qobuz genres (paged). Use this as the entrypoint for genre-based browsing.
tools.tools_settings_list: List Settings subsections from Home (e.g., Profile, Display Settings)
tools.tools_settings_display_list: Read Settings → Display Settings (titles + current state)
tools.tools_settings_profile_set: Set the current Profile (executes the Profile action node and confirms selection)
tools.tools_genre_artists_list: List Artists within a Genre (paged). Use this BEFORE opening a specific artist with tools_artist_open. Read-only.
tools.tools_genre_albums_list: List Albums within a Genre (paged). Use this BEFORE opening a specific album. Read-only.
tools.tools_tidal_open: Open the TIDAL hub (service tiles such as What’s New, Rising, Playlists, Genres, Your Favorites). This is the recommended entrypoint for browsing TIDAL content. Always reuse the sessionId from this card for follow-up calls (sections, typed lists, node_open).
tools.tools_tidal_section_open: Open a TIDAL tile and optionally list a known sub-section (albums/playlists/tracks). Use this to drill into a specific TIDAL shelf using the sessionId from tools_tidal_open. Prefer this over ad-hoc node navigation when a typed section is available; fall back to tools_node_open only if the typed section is empty or unavailable.
tools.tools_tidal_albums_list: List TIDAL albums from a specific section (paged). Use this after tools_tidal_open or tools_tidal_section_open with the same sessionId and nodeKey. Prefer this typed list for deterministic album browsing before opening an album via tools_album_open.
tools.tools_tidal_playlists_list: List TIDAL playlists from a specific section (paged). Use this after tools_tidal_open or tools_tidal_section_open with the same sessionId and nodeKey. Prefer playlist-level tools (tools_playlist_open / tools_playlist_play_now) once a playlist is selected.
tools.tools_tidal_tracks_list: List TIDAL tracks from a specific section (paged). Use this after tools_tidal_open or tools_tidal_section_open with the same sessionId and nodeKey. For an individual track, open it with tools_track_open and execute via tools_track_play_now / tools_track_add_next / tools_track_queue.
tools.tools_qobuz_open: Open the Qobuz hub (tiles such as What’s New, Taste of Qobuz, Your Favorites). This is the recommended entrypoint for browsing Qobuz content. Always reuse the sessionId from this card for Qobuz section/list calls and node_open navigation.
tools.tools_qobuz_section_open: Open a Qobuz tile and optionally list a known sub-section (albums/playlists/tracks). Use this to drill into a Qobuz shelf using the sessionId from tools_qobuz_open. Typed section readers may be inconsistent on some cores/regions; when a typed section is empty, fall back to tools_node_open on the same nodeKey instead of retrying blindly.
tools.tools_qobuz_albums_list: List Qobuz albums from a specific section (paged). Use this after tools_qobuz_open or tools_qobuz_section_open with the same sessionId and nodeKey. If this typed list is empty, follow the tool advice to try tools_node_open instead of retrying blindly.
tools.tools_qobuz_playlists_list: List Qobuz playlists from a specific section (paged). Use this after tools_qobuz_open or tools_qobuz_section_open. Once you select a playlist, prefer playlist-level tools (tools_playlist_open / tools_playlist_play_now).
tools.tools_qobuz_tracks_list: List Qobuz tracks from a specific section (paged). Use this after tools_qobuz_open or tools_qobuz_section_open. For a chosen track, open it with tools_track_open and execute via tools_track_play_now / tools_track_add_next / tools_track_queue.
tools.tools_playlist_preflight: Preflight a set of playlist or track items to determine can_addnext / can_queue semantics. Helps construct playlist plans and avoid invalid per-track loops.
tools.tools_capabilities: Return RWAV Bridge capabilities, including available tool groups and features. Use this early in a session to understand available playback, queue, search, streaming and device features.
tools.tools_album_preflight: Preflight an album for Add Next / Queue (read-only)
tools.tools_history_artists_list: List history artists (read-only; search optional). Use this to explore played artists in history/analytics views; does not control playback.
tools.tools_history_artist_get: Get a history artist record by id (read-only). Use this to inspect analytics metadata about an artist; not for playback control.
tools.tools_history_albums_list: List history albums (read-only; filter by artistId/search). Use this for analytics/history browsing, not for controlling playback.
tools.tools_history_album_get: Get history album by id (read-only). Use this to inspect a played album record; not for playback control.
tools.tools_history_tracks_list: List tracks from the RWAV history database (read-only), with optional filters by albumId/artistId/search. Use this to inspect what has been played over time, not to control playback.
tools.tools_history_track_get: Get a single history track record by id (read-only). Use this to inspect metadata about a track that has been played, not for playback control.
tools.tools_history_plays_list: List plays (listening events) with filters + paging (zoneId/trackId/date range). Read-only analytics; use this for reporting or visualisation of listening history, not for controlling playback.
tools.tools_history_play_get: Get a single play event by id (history record). Read-only; exposes when/what played, not a way to replay it.
tools.tools_snapshots_recently_played: Get a snapshot of recently played items (scope=all|zone). Read-only analytics for building “recently played” views, not for modifying the queue.
tools.tools_snapshots_most_played_tracks: Get a snapshot of most played tracks (optionally scoped by zone and date range). Read-only analytics useful for “most played” charts, not for queue control.
tools.tools_snapshots_most_played_artists: Get a snapshot of most played artists (optionally scoped by zone and date range). Read-only analytics, suitable for top-artist views.
tools.tools_snapshots_most_played_albums: Get a snapshot of most played albums (optionally scoped by zone and date range). Read-only analytics for surfacing favourite albums.
tools.tools_snapshots_listening_time_daily: Get a snapshot of listening time per day (optionally scoped by zone and date range). Purely read-only analytics, intended for charts/usage insights.
tools.tools_snapshots_track_first_last: Get first/last play timestamps for a given trackId. Read-only analytics; use this for “when did I first/last play this?” insights.
tools.tools_instructions_startup: Return the RWAV startup instructions and global usage rules. This is the main reference for safe, efficient use of RWAV tools (search-first, session reuse, execute-once-then-verify, queue head/tail helpers, streaming fallbacks, volume safety).
tools.tools_discovery: Return all public RWAV tools and metadata. This is the main entrypoint for MPC tool discovery. Use this to enumerate available functionality, then follow specific navigation/playback/search tools as needed.
tools.tools_playlists_drafts_create: Create an in-memory playlist draft (transient). Use this as an alternative to playlist_plan when building multi-item sets. Execute via tools_playlists_execute; do not issue per-track operations.
tools.tools_playlists_drafts_get: Retrieve an in-memory playlist draft. Read-only; used for inspection before executing the draft.
tools.tools_playlists_drafts_update: Update an in-memory playlist draft (add/remove/reorder items). Execute via tools_playlists_execute only once per intent.
tools.tools_playlists_drafts_delete: Delete an in-memory playlist draft. Used to clean up transient plans.
tools.tools_playlists_execute: Execute an in-memory playlist draft using append/addnext semantics. On addnext, use pause_for_addnext to control final zone state: false restores the original play/pause state (non‑disruptive), true allows the zone to remain paused; omitted preserves current behaviour. Optional de‑dupe drops unintended duplicates within the draft and near the insertion window. Idempotent within TTL. Execute ONCE, then verify via recommended head/tail helpers.
tools.tools_zones_list: List zones (public surface; wrapper over list_zones)
tools.tools_outputs_list: List outputs for a given zone or all outputs on the Core, mapping output_id to display name. Read-only helper used before volume/mute/grouping operations.
tools.tools_outputs_list_group_candidates: List outputs that can be grouped with a primary output (based on can_group_with_output_ids). Use this before tools_group_zones or tools_outputs_group to avoid illegal groupings.
tools.tools_outputs_group: Group outputs under a primary output (local RAAT grouping). Requires a primary_output_id and one or more output_ids that are compatible. Use tools_outputs_list_group_candidates first.
tools.tools_outputs_ungroup: Ungroup outputs (per-output fallback). Use this to break groups where tools_group_zones or tools_outputs_group were used. Read the results array to see which outputs succeeded.
tools.tools_group_zones: Group outputs into a single zone (cloud-style grouping). Requires 2+ output_ids that are mutually groupable via can_group_with_output_ids. Use tools_outputs_list and tools_outputs_list_group_candidates before calling this.
tools.tools_playlist_capabilities: Report playlist capabilities (addnext/append/play/shuffle). Use this BEFORE executing operations to ensure the platform supports the requested action.
tools.tools_playlist_plan: Create a transient playlist plan for bulk Add Next or Queue operations. Use this when you have multiple items or queries; do NOT call track_add_next or track_queue repeatedly. Execute once via tools_playlist_execute, then verify via head/tail snapshots (tools_queue_head_get or tools_queue_tail_get).
tools.tools_playlist_execute: Execute a transient playlist plan (append or addnext) in a single operation. On addnext, use pause_for_addnext to control final zone state: false restores the original play/pause state (non‑disruptive), true allows the zone to remain paused after queue surgery; when omitted, current behaviour is preserved. Optional de‑dupe drops unintended duplicates within the plan and near the insertion window. You may override the plan strategy at execution by passing strategy (useful after previewing the plan). Execute ONCE, then verify via queue head/tail as advised.
tools.tools_job_status_get: Get status of an asynchronous job
tools.tools_ungroup_output: Ungroup a specific output from any group
tools.tools_transfer_playback: Transfer playback (track, queue context, position, and state) to another zone. Playback state is preserved by the Core: if the source was playing, the destination will be playing; if paused, it remains paused. Do not auto‑toggle play/pause after transfer — verify via tools_now_playing_get before any transport actions.
tools.tools_library_albums_list: List Library → Albums (paged). Use this to browse Library albums, then open a selected album with tools_album_open for actions and playback. Read-only browser, not a playback action.
tools.tools_library_artists_list: List Library → Artists (paged). Use this to browse Library artists, then open a selected artist with tools_artist_open. Read-only; artist-level actions are performed via tools_artist_open and tools_artist_play_now.
tools.tools_library_composers_list: List Library → Composers (paged). Use this to browse Library composers, then open a specific composer via tools_composer_open for actions (Play/Shuffle/Radio). Read-only navigation.
tools.tools_library_tracks_list: List Library → Tracks (paged). Use this when you need a broad view of Library tracks. For targeted playback, prefer search-first flows (tools_search_run or tools_track_search_open) plus tools_track_open/tools_track_play_now.
tools.tools_library_tags_list: List Library → Tags (paged). Use this to discover available tags, then open a tag with tools_tag_open for actions and rows.
tools.tools_tag_open: Open a Library Tag and return actions (Shuffle, Start Radio) plus optional track/album rows. Use this to explore tagged content. If the tag resolves to an owner action_list, open that owner and execute the child action via tools_play_by_key. Prefer tag-level actions over iterating individual tracks or albums.
tools.tools_tag_play_now: Start tag playback via Shuffle or Radio. Single-shot action; execute once and verify via tools_now_playing_get. Do not iterate track rows unless the user selects a specific item.
tools.tools_library_playlists_list: List Library → Playlists (paged). Use this to browse Library playlists, then open a playlist with tools_playlist_open. Prefer playlist-level actions (Play Now/Add Next/Queue) over per-track iteration.
tools.tools_library_playlists_pick: Pick N Library → Playlists items and return action-ready entries.
tools.tools_playlist_open: Open a playlist and retrieve playlist actions (Play Now, Shuffle, Add Next, Queue, Start Radio) and track rows. Prefer playlist-level actions to per-track actions. If the playlist is a curated wrapper, detect the owner action_list and use tools_play_by_key for execution.
tools.tools_playlist_search_open: Search for playlists, then open a playlist with fresh session context. Use this to avoid stale playlistKeys. After opening, prefer playlist-level actions to row-level iteration.
tools.tools_playlist_open_simple: Open a Library/TIDAL/Qobuz playlist using a simple title or playlistKey, resolving owner action_list keys. Useful for curated wrappers; always use playlist-level actions from the returned card.
tools.tools_playlist_play_now_simple: Start playlist playback immediately. This is a playlist-level action; do NOT loop per-track. Verify playback with tools_now_playing_get (and tools_queue_head_get if needed).
tools.tools_playlist_play_now: Start playlist playback immediately. This is a playlist-level action; do NOT loop per-track. Verify playback with tools_now_playing_get (and tools_queue_head_get if needed). If reason:"curated_wrapper" is returned, open the owner via tools_node_open and execute the child action via tools_play_by_key. Do NOT iterate track rows for curated playlists.
tools.tools_playlist_shuffle: Start playlist playback immediately. This is a playlist-level action; do NOT loop per-track. Verify playback with tools_now_playing_get (and tools_queue_head_get if needed).
tools.tools_playlist_add_next: Add an entire playlist immediately after the current track. Execute ONCE per intent and verify via tools_queue_head_get. If duplicate within idempotency TTL, perform verification only (do NOT re-inject). If reason:"curated_wrapper" is returned, open the owner via tools_node_open and execute the child action via tools_play_by_key. Do NOT iterate track rows for curated playlists.
tools.tools_playlist_queue: Append a playlist to the tail of the queue. Execute ONCE per intent; verify via tools_queue_tail_get. Use playlist-level actions rather than adding tracks individually. If reason:"curated_wrapper" is returned, open the owner via tools_node_open and execute the child action via tools_play_by_key. Do NOT iterate track rows for curated playlists.
tools.tools_playlist_start_radio: Start a radio session from the playlist. Stateless one-shot action; no need to iterate track rows. Verify playback state via tools_now_playing_get.
tools.tools_playlist_track_open: Open a specific playlist track and return a per‑track actions card
tools.tools_playlist_play_from_here: Play From Here for a track inside a playlist. Execute ONCE, then verify via tools_now_playing_get and/or tools_queue_head_get. This tool is idempotent within TTL; duplicate calls MUST trigger verification only, not a new injection.
tools.tools_playlist_track_play_now: Play a specific track inside a playlist. Verify playback with tools_now_playing_get. Use ONLY when the user explicitly requests a single track from the playlist.
tools.tools_playlist_track_add_next: Add a specific playlist track immediately next. Verify via tools_queue_head_get. Avoid using this for whole-playlist Add Next; prefer tools_playlist_add_next.
tools.tools_playlist_track_queue: Append a specific playlist track to the queue. Verify via tools_queue_tail_get. Avoid per-track queueing when a playlist-level action is available.
tools.tools_playlist_track_start_radio: Start a radio session from this playlist track. Use only when the user selects a specific track. Verify via tools_now_playing_get.
tools.tools_now_playing_get: Get a Now Playing snapshot for the effective zone (state, title/artist/album, position, volume, outputs). Use this to verify the result of playback and transport actions (play/pause/seek/shuffle/repeat/auto_radio) before deciding to retry anything.
tools.tools_now_playing_playpause: Toggle play/pause for the current zone. This is a simple transport toggle; execute once and verify state via tools_now_playing_get instead of sending repeated toggles.
tools.tools_now_playing_next: Skip to the next track in the queue for the current zone. Execute once, then verify via tools_now_playing_get or tools_queue_head_get.
tools.tools_now_playing_previous: Skip to the previous track in the queue for the current zone. Execute once, then verify via tools_now_playing_get.
tools.tools_now_playing_seek: Seek to an absolute position (ms) in the current track. Validates against track length when available and clamps near the end by default. Execute once and verify via tools_now_playing_get instead of issuing repeated seeks.
tools.tools_now_playing_shuffle: Set shuffle mode on/off for the current zone. Execute once and verify via tools_zone_settings_get or tools_now_playing_get. Be aware that Auto Radio may override shuffle behaviour.
tools.tools_now_playing_repeat: Set repeat mode for the current zone (off/one/all). Some Cores expect track/queue semantics; this tool normalizes both. Execute once and verify via tools_zone_settings_get. If the Core rejects repeat, use the advice to adjust Auto Radio or settings instead of re-sending repeat blindly.
tools.tools_zone_settings_get: Read per-zone playback settings (loop/shuffle/auto_radio). Use this to verify the effect of shuffle/repeat/auto_radio tools and to understand why some transport actions may be ignored.
tools.tools_now_playing_auto_radio: Enable or disable Auto Radio (Roon Radio) for the current zone. Auto Radio can override shuffle/repeat behaviour; execute once and verify via tools_zone_settings_get or tools_now_playing_get.
tools.tools_queue_get: Get the full current queue snapshot for verification and UI sync. Heavier than head/tail helpers; use after tools_queue_head_get or tools_queue_tail_get when results are ambiguous.
tools.tools_queue_play_from_here: Move playback to a specific queue row (Play From Here). Execute this ONCE per intent, then verify via tools_now_playing_get and/or tools_queue_head_get. This tool is idempotent within a short TTL; do not re-issue it repeatedly.
tools.tools_volume_adjust: Adjust volume by a small delta (default ±3) with safety guards. Requires zoneId (and outputId when a zone has multiple outputs). Execute once per intent and, if needed, verify via tools_now_playing_get or tools_outputs_list. Volume >85 requires allow_high_volume=true.
tools.tools_volume_set: Set absolute volume (0–100) with safety guards. Requires zoneId (and outputId for multi-output zones). Changes >10 points require allow_large_change=true; targets >85 require allow_high_volume=true. Execute once and verify via tools_now_playing_get if needed.
tools.tools_mute: Mute a specific output in a zone. Requires zoneId (and outputId when a zone has multiple outputs). Execute once and verify via tools_now_playing_get; do not loop mute calls if verification is pending.
tools.tools_unmute: Unmute a specific output in a zone. Requires zoneId (and outputId for multi-output zones). Execute once and verify via tools_now_playing_get.
tools.tools_mute_all: Mute all outputs on the Core (global). Execute once and verify by inspecting zones via tools_zones_list or tools_now_playing_get. Intended for emergency/quick silence operations; do not loop.
tools.tools_unmute_all: Unmute all outputs on the Core (global). Execute once and verify via tools_zones_list. Intended for restoring normal playback; do not loop.
tools.tools_search_run: Search and return a sectioned list card
tools.tools_image_resolve: Build artwork URLs for an image_key (original and thumbnail)
tools.tools_album_open: Open an album and return a card with actions (Play Now, Add Next, Queue, Start Radio) and track rows. Prefer this as the main entrypoint for album playback. For per-track operations on this album, use tools_album_track_open and tools_album_track_execute instead of generic track queries.
tools.tools_album_play_now: Play an album now. Single-shot action; do not loop. Verify playback via tools_now_playing_get. For further operations on the same album, reuse album context (tools_album_open) rather than re-searching.
tools.tools_album_add_next: Add an album immediately after the current track. Execute ONCE per intent and verify via tools_queue_head_get. Zero queue delta is not an immediate failure; use head/tail helpers for confirmation rather than re-running the action.
tools.tools_album_queue: Append an album at the end of the queue. Execute ONCE per intent and verify via tools_queue_tail_get. If verification shows no change, use tools_queue_get once; do not call tools_album_queue repeatedly.
tools.tools_album_start_radio: Start a radio session for this album. Stateless one-shot action; do not loop. Verify playback state via tools_now_playing_get when needed.
tools.tools_track_open: Open a track and return a card with actions (Play Now, Add Next, Queue, Start Radio). Use this after search or list selection. Prefer using the actions from this card instead of constructing new queries by hand.
tools.tools_track_play_now: Play a specific track now. This is a single-shot action. Verify playback via tools_now_playing_get; do not loop play operations for the same track.
tools.tools_track_add_next: Add a specific track immediately after the current track. Execute ONCE per user intent and verify via tools_queue_head_get (head_then_full). accepted:true is returned only when a change is confirmed (or idempotent_verified). If pending_confirmation + zero delta, verify-only; do not retry.
tools.tools_track_queue: Append a specific track at the end of the queue. Execute ONCE per user intent and verify via tools_queue_tail_get (tail_then_full). accepted:true is returned only when a change is confirmed (or idempotent_verified). If pending_confirmation + zero delta, verify-only; do not retry. Use playlist/plan tools for bulk queueing instead of repeated per-track calls.
tools.tools_track_start_radio: Start a radio session based on this track. Stateless one-shot action; verify playback with tools_now_playing_get if needed. Use when the user explicitly wants radio from a specific track.
tools.tools_track_execute_by_query: Execute a track operation by query (play/addnext/queue/radio) in the Library. Best used when the query is unambiguous (e.g., a known Library track). For general flows, prefer tools_track_search_open or tools_track_operation, and fall back to album context (tools_album_open → tools_album_track_execute) when advised.
tools.tools_album_track_open: Open a specific track within an album and return per-track actions. Use this when you already have album context (from tools_album_open). This is the preferred way to operate on album tracks, especially for TIDAL/Qobuz and variants.
tools.tools_album_track_execute: Execute a track action within an album context (play/addnext/queue/radio). Preferred safe path when working with album tracks, especially for streaming services. Strict per-row selection (index, then exact normalized title). Returns executed_track diagnostics on success. Execute ONCE; verify via tools_now_playing_get (play/radio) or queue head/tail (addnext/queue).
tools.tools_track_search_open: Search for a track and return an action_list card (Play Now, Add Next, Queue, Start Radio). This is the recommended entrypoint for track operations from natural language queries. Prefer this over tools_track_execute_by_query for ambiguous or streaming content.
tools.tools_track_operation: Execute a track operation with smart fallback: first by track_item_key, then by album context (album_key/title+artist+track), and finally by query. Preferred when you need a robust track execution pipeline. Execute once and follow the verification hints in the response; do not manually re-run lower-level operations.
tools.tools_artist_open: Open an Artist hub using name or artistKey, returning actions (Play Artist, Shuffle, Start Radio), Albums and Top Tracks. Always reuse the sessionId from this card for follow-up calls. For playback, prefer artist-level actions rather than looping through individual tracks. Curated wrappers may appear; use tools_node_open + tools_play_by_key when needed.
tools.tools_composer_open: Open a Composer hub and return actions (Play, Shuffle, Radio) and Works. Reuse the sessionId from this card for follow-up calls. When a composer exposes a curated owner action_list, open the owner via tools_node_open and execute child actions via tools_play_by_key. Prefer composer-level actions unless the user explicitly wants a specific work.
tools.tools_composer_play_now: Play a Composer (Play, Shuffle). Execute once and verify via tools_now_playing_get. Do not iterate Works unless the user explicitly selects a specific work.
tools.tools_composer_start_radio: Start Composer Radio. One-shot; verify via tools_now_playing_get.
tools.tools_work_open: Open a Work (owner action list) and return a normalized actions card
tools.tools_composer_list_works: List Works for this composer (paged). Use this BEFORE selecting an individual Work or Recording. Read-only.
tools.tools_artist_play_now: Play an Artist (Play, Shuffle, or Radio). Execute a single artist-level action. Verify via tools_now_playing_get. Do not iterate Top Tracks row-by-row unless the user directly selects one.
tools.tools_artist_start_radio: Start Artist Radio. One-shot action; verify playback with tools_now_playing_get.
tools.tools_artist_get_albums: List albums for this artist. Use this BEFORE opening a specific album with tools_album_open. Read-only browser; does not start playback.
tools.tools_artist_get_top_tracks: List Top Tracks for this artist (read-only). For playback, open a specific track via tools_track_open or use artist-level actions.
tools.tools_track_variants_open: Search a track and present canonical and variant versions (live/remix/remaster/alternate). Use this when the user cares which version is played. After selection, use tools_track_play_now/add_next/queue on the chosen variant.
tools.tools_track_open_batch_by_query: Open multiple per-track action cards for a list of queries. Use this to prefetch actions for several tracks at once, then execute play/addnext/queue per track from the returned cards instead of building raw queries repeatedly.
tools.tools_library_tracks_pick: Pick N Library tracks and return action-ready entries (with normalized actions). Use this to sample tracks from the Library without running full search queries, then queue them via playlist/plan tools or per-track actions.
tools.tools_genre_tracks_pick: Pick N tracks from a Genre and return action-ready entries. Useful for building genre-based sets before queueing them with playlist/plan or per-track tools.
tools.tools_artist_add_next: Add the Artist’s tracks or selections next in queue. Execute ONCE and verify via tools_queue_head_get. Prefer this over looping through Top Tracks individually.
tools.tools_artist_queue: Append Artist content to the end of the queue. Execute ONCE and verify via tools_queue_tail_get. Use artist-level actions instead of adding each track manually.
tools.tools_genre_open: Open a Genre hub, returning sub-genres, artists, albums and actions (Play Genre, Start Radio). Prefer genre-level playback over iterating through individual tracks unless the user explicitly selects an item.
tools.tools_genre_start_radio: Start Radio from this genre. One-shot action; verify playback state with tools_now_playing_get.
tools.tools_live_radio_play_now: Play a Live Radio station now
tools.tools_play_by_key: Navigate a node by item_key (starts action nodes)

Returns fully working code with comments and example usage. NOTE: Code is template-based, not generated from documentation - always verify against current API docs.

tools.evaluateInsight:
Evaluate the long-term value and significance of an insight or thought based on the following criteria: 
      1. Actionability (1-10): Can this be applied to future work? Is there any information that can be used to apply this thought to future work in different contexts? Is the problem it solves clear?
      2. Longevity (1-10): Will this be relevant months or years from now?
      3. Findability (1-10): Would this be hard to rediscover if forgotten?
      4. Future Reference Value (1-10): How likely are you to need this again?
      
      Insights to ignore: 
      1. Trivial syntax details
      2. Redundant information
tools.rollup:
Synthesize my daily note to create an organized rollup of the most important notes with clear categories, connections, and action items. Optionally specify a date (YYYY-MM-DD).
       Only include notes that actually add long-term value. If you are unsure, call the /evaluateInsight tool to evaluate the long-term value of the thought.
       If you do not have enough information, stop and ask the user for more information.
       It is better to not log anything than log something that is not useful.
tools.write_note: Create a new note or overwrite an existing note with content. Path should be relative to your notes directory. Optionally include tags that will be merged with any existing tags in the note.
tools.search_files: Recursively search for files and directories matching a pattern in your notes directory. The search is case-insensitive and matches partial names. Returns full paths to all matching items. Great for finding notes when you don't know their exact location.
tools.read_note: Read the complete contents of a note file from your notes directory. Specify the path relative to your notes directory (e.g., 'Log/2023-01-01.md'). Returns the full text content of the note file.
tools.read_multiple_notes: Read the contents of multiple note files simultaneously. Specify paths relative to your notes directory (e.g., ['Log/2023-01-01.md', 'Rollups/2023-01-01-rollup.md']). Returns each file's content with its path as a reference.
tools.list_directory: List the contents of a directory in your notes. Shows all files and directories with clear labels. Specify path relative to your notes directory (e.g., 'Log' or 'Rollups').
tools.create_directory: Create a new directory in your notes. Can create nested directories in one operation. Path should be relative to your notes directory.

tools.searchContacts: Search for contacts and return matching people. Use for questions about specific contacts or "who" questions (e.g. "Who did I meet most?" or "who works as an engineer?"). Returns actual contact records for queries needing specific people.
tools.searchInteractions: Search for interactions and return matching interactions. Use for questions about specific interactions, "who" questions (e.g. "Who did I meet most?"), finding best friends based on relevance score, or finding recently added/created contacts. Returns actual contact records for queries needing specific interactions.
tools.aggregateContacts: Get numerical statistics and counts ONLY. Returns numbers and percentages, never specific contacts. For counting questions like "how many work at Google?" or "what % are engineers?". Use search endpoint instead for any "who" questions or to get actual contact details.
tools.getContact: Get details for a contact by id, including emails, social links, phone numbers, and notes.
tools.createContact: Create a new contact record in Clay. This endpoint should only be used when you need to create a completely new contact, not for adding contacts to groups.
tools.createNote: Create a note for a contact. Only use this when the user explicitly asks to create, add, or save a note.
tools.getGroups: Get all groups or lists for the user.
tools.createGroup: Create a group or list for the user. If a group with the same name already exists, it will not create a duplicate unless explicitly requested to ignore the check.
tools.updateGroup: Update a group or list. Use this to update the group title and/or modify its members. When adding or removing contacts, provide ALL contact IDs to add/remove in a single call - do not make multiple calls for individual contacts.
tools.getNotes: Use ONLY when the user explicitly mentions "note" or "notes" to retrieve notes between two dates (e.g. "what notes from last week?"). Returns notes by creation date only - does NOT search note content or filter by other criteria. NEVER use this tool for finding contacts or any other purpose besides retrieving notes. This tool is strictly prohibited from being used unless "note" or "notes" are explicitly mentioned in the query.
tools.getEvents: Use this tool ONLY to fetch meetings/events in a date range (e.g. "what meetings next week?", "show calendar for tomorrow"). DO NOT use for counting meetings, analyzing patterns, or finding frequent participants.

Returns a list of all users.
The users are returned sorted by creation date, with the newest users appearing first.
tools.CreateUser:
Creates a new user. Your user management settings determine how you should setup your user model.

Any email address and phone number created using this method will be marked as verified.

Note: If you are performing a migration, check out our guide on [zero downtime migrations](https://clerk.com/docs/deployments/migrate-overview).

A rate limit rule of 20 requests per 10 seconds is applied to this endpoint.
tools.GetUsersCount: Returns a total count of all users that match the given filtering criteria.
tools.GetUser: Retrieve the details of a user
tools.UpdateUser:
Update a user's attributes.

You can set the user's primary contact identifiers (email address and phone numbers) by updating the `primary_email_address_id` and `primary_phone_number_id` attributes respectively.
Both IDs should correspond to verified identifications that belong to the user.

You can remove a user's username by setting the username attribute to null or the blank string "".
This is a destructive action; the identification will be deleted forever.
Usernames can be removed only if they are optional in your instance settings and there's at least one other identifier which can be used for authentication.

This endpoint allows changing a user's password. When passing the `password` parameter directly you have two further options.
You can ignore the password policy checks for your instance by setting the `skip_password_checks` parameter to `true`.
You can also choose to sign the user out of all their active sessions on any device once the password is updated. Just set `sign_out_of_other_sessions` to `true`.
tools.BanUser: Marks the given user as banned, which means that all their sessions are revoked and they are not allowed to sign in again.
tools.ListInvitations: Returns all non-revoked invitations for your application, sorted by creation date
tools.CreateInvitation:
Creates a new invitation for the given email address and sends the invitation email.
Keep in mind that you cannot create an invitation if there is already one for the given email address.
Also, trying to create an invitation for an email address that already exists in your application will result to an error.
tools.RevokeInvitation:
Revokes the given invitation.
Revoking an invitation will prevent the user from using the invitation link that was sent to them.
However, it doesn't prevent the user from signing up if they follow the sign up flow.
Only active (i.e. non-revoked) invitations can be revoked.
tools.ListDomains:
Use this endpoint to get a list of all domains for an instance.
The response will contain the primary domain for the instance and any satellite domains. Each domain in the response contains information about the URLs where Clerk operates and the required CNAME targets.

tools.getFigjamContent:
Get content from a Figjam board. 

Example URL: https://www.figma.com/board/{file-id}/{board-name}?node-id={node-id}

The URL format is:
- Base: https://www.figma.com/board/
- File ID: The string after /board/ and before the next / or ?
- Node ID: Found in the URL parameter 'node-id', but IMPORTANT: Replace the hyphen (-) with a colon (:)

For example:
- If URL has node-id=173-240, use nodeId="173:240"
- If URL has node-id=0-1, use nodeId="0:1"
- If there is no node-id, use nodeId="0:1"

Important Notes:
- Always provide a nodeId parameter
- When a user asks about a FigJam board in general without specifying a node, use nodeId="0:1"
- When the link contains node-id=0-1 or node-id=0:1, use nodeId="0:1" as this refers to the entire board/file
- The Figma API requires node IDs to use colons (:) instead of hyphens (-), always convert hyphens to colons

Note: The Figma API requires node IDs to use colons (:) instead of hyphens (-). 
Always convert hyphens to colons when making API requests.
tools.getFigjamNodes:
Get specific nodes from a Figjam board.

Example URL: https://www.figma.com/board/asdf1234/example-board?node-id=0-1

URL Structure:
- Figjam URLs always start with 'https://www.figma.com/board/'
- The file ID comes after '/board/' (in this case 'asdf1234')
- Node IDs in the API use colons (:) not hyphens (-). Example: '173:240' not '173-240'

Node Types:
Common node types you might want to filter for include:
- STICKY: Sticky notes
- SHAPE: Basic shapes
- TEXT: Text elements
- CONNECTOR: Connection lines
- FRAME: Frames/containers

You can specify one or more node types to filter the results.
tools.getFigjamComments:
Get all comments from a Figjam board.

Example URL: https://www.figma.com/board/asdf1234/example-board

The URL format is:
- Base: https://www.figma.com/board/
- File ID: The string after /board/ and before the next / or ?

This tool will return:
- All comments in the file
- Comment metadata (author, timestamp, etc.)
- Node information if the comment is attached to a specific node
- Resolution status of comments

Note: Comments are returned in chronological order, with the oldest comments first.

tools.check_app_in_browser:
Give an AI agent eyes on a live website or app. The agent browses it, interacts with it, and tells you whether a given task or check passed. Works on localhost or any URL. Use for visual QA, flow validation, regression checks, or anything that needs a real browser to verify.

LOCALHOST SUPPORT: Pass any localhost URL (e.g. http://localhost:3000) and it Just Works. A secure tunnel is automatically created so the remote browser can reach your local dev server — no manual ngrok setup, no port forwarding, no config.

SCOPE PER CALL: Keep each call to ONE focused check — a single page or a short interaction on a single screen (login, submit a form, verify a heading). For anything spanning multiple pages or long multi-step flows, split into SEPARATE calls — the remote browser agent has a ~25-step internal budget per call, and long single calls risk client-side timeouts. Example: instead of "log in, then go to settings, then update profile, then verify," make three calls: (1) log in & verify dashboard, (2) update settings, (3) verify profile change.

CREDENTIALS: pass them as PARAMETERS, not only in the description. Naming an account in `description` alone does not make the agent use it — it falls back to the environment's stored credential. Use `username`/`password` (or `credentialId`) for the run's identity, `auth.username`/`auth.password` to pin the precondition login, and `loginCredentials` for accounts the agent must use at a login form it hits PART-WAY through the task (e.g. set a password → bounced to sign-in → log in as the account you just created). Anything you specify beats the environment's default for every login in the run; the result reports the identity actually used under `logins`.
tools.probe_page:
Probe one or more URLs and return their rendered state — screenshot, page metadata (title/finalUrl/statusCode/loadTimeMs), structured console errors, and per-URL network summary (refetch loops collapse into one row by origin+pathname).

WHEN TO USE: "did I just break /settings?" / "smoke-test these 5 routes after my refactor" / "what's actually rendering at /dashboard?" — fast (<10s for 1 URL, <25s for 20), no LLM cost, no agent loop.

NOT FOR: scenario verification (sign in → click X → assert Y), interaction (clicks, form fills, scrolls), or anything requiring agent decisions. Use check_app_in_browser for those.

LOCALHOST SUPPORT: any localhost URL is auto-tunneled. Pre-flight TCP probe fails fast (<2s) if the dev server isn't listening.

BATCH MODE: pass up to 20 targets in one call to share browser session + tunnel — dramatically faster than firing parallel single-URL probes (one execution unit, not N). Per-URL waitForSelector / waitForLoadState / timeoutMs override defaults.

A single failed target's error appears in result.error without failing the whole batch — the other results stay valid.
tools.trigger_crawl:
Trigger a browser-agent crawl of a web app to build the project's knowledge graph. The crawl systematically explores pages, UI states, and navigation flows, then populates the backend's knowledge graph so future evaluations and tests have context about the app.

LOCALHOST SUPPORT: Pass any localhost URL (e.g. http://localhost:3000) and it Just Works. A secure tunnel is automatically created so the remote browser can reach your local dev server.

WHEN TO USE: after a significant new feature, a new environment, or when onboarding a project. NOT for per-change verification — use check_app_in_browser for that.

SCOPE: one crawl per call against one URL. The crawl is long-running (minutes to tens of minutes depending on app size) and populates backend state asynchronously; the tool returns the execution status once the workflow completes. This does NOT return pass/fail — it returns executionId + status + outcome.
tools.project:
Manage DebuggAI projects. Pass an "action":
  - "get"    {uuid} → one project with full detail.
  - "list"   {q?, page?, pageSize?} → paginated project summaries.
  - "create" {name, platform, (teamUuid|teamName), (repoUuid|repoName)} → create a project. The repo must be GitHub-linked; names resolve by case-insensitive exact match.

Note: there is no update/delete here — rename/delete a project from the DebuggAI web app.
tools.environment:
Manage environments (and their login credentials) under a project. Pass an "action":
  - "get"    {uuid, projectUuid?} → one environment with credentials inline (passwords never returned).
  - "list"   {projectUuid?, q?, page?, pageSize?} → paginated environments. projectUuid auto-resolves from the git repo if omitted.
  - "create" {name, url, description?, projectUuid?, credentials?} → create an env, optionally seeding credentials.
  - "update" {uuid, name?, url?, description?, addCredentials?, updateCredentials?, removeCredentialIds?} → patch env + manage credentials.
  - "delete" {uuid, projectUuid?, confirm?} → delete env (DESTRUCTIVE; requires confirmation).
tools.test_suite:
Manage and run test suites. Identify a suite by suiteUuid, or suiteName + a project identifier (projectUuid|projectName). Pass an "action":
  - "list"    {projectUuid|projectName, search?, page?, pageSize?} → paginated suites with status/pass-rate.
  - "create"  {name, description, projectUuid|projectName} → create a suite.
  - "run"     {suiteUuid|(suiteName+project), targetUrl?} → run all tests async. Poll with action:"results".
  - "results" {suiteUuid|(suiteName+project)} → suite + per-test outcomes.
  - "delete"  {suiteUuid|(suiteName+project), confirm?} → soft-delete (DESTRUCTIVE; requires confirmation).
tools.test_case:
Manage individual test cases within a suite. Pass an "action":
  - "create" {name, description, agentTaskDescription, suiteUuid|(suiteName+project), relativeUrl?, maxSteps?} → add a test case (NOT auto-run).
  - "update" {testUuid, name?, description?, agentTaskDescription?} → patch a test case.
  - "delete" {testUuid, confirm?} → soft-delete (DESTRUCTIVE; requires confirmation).
tools.executions:
Look up workflow executions (history of check_app_in_browser, trigger_crawl, and test-suite runs). Pass an "action":
  - "get"  {uuid} → one execution with FULL detail (nodeExecutions, state, errorInfo) + any screenshot/gif artifacts.
  - "list" {projectUuid?, status?, page?, pageSize?} → paginated execution summaries. status ∈ completed|running|failed|cancelled|pending.

Tip: after a fresh check_app_in_browser run, poll action:"get" with the returned executionId until artifact URLs are available.

tools.salesforce_search_objects: Search for Salesforce standard and custom objects by name pattern. Examples: 'Account' will find Account, AccountHistory; 'Order' will find WorkOrder, ServiceOrder__c etc.
tools.salesforce_describe_object: Get detailed schema metadata including all fields, relationships, and field properties of any Salesforce object. Examples: 'Account' shows all Account fields including custom fields; 'Case' shows all Case fields including relationships to Account, Contact etc.
tools.salesforce_query_records:
Query records from any Salesforce object using SOQL, including relationship queries.

NOTE: For queries with GROUP BY, aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, etc.), or HAVING clauses, use salesforce_aggregate_query instead.

Examples:
1. Parent-to-child query (e.g., Account with Contacts):
   - objectName: "Account"
   - fields: ["Name", "(SELECT Id, FirstName, LastName FROM Contacts)"]

2. Child-to-parent query (e.g., Contact with Account details):
   - objectName: "Contact"
   - fields: ["FirstName", "LastName", "Account.Name", "Account.Industry"]

3. Multiple level query (e.g., Contact -> Account -> Owner):
   - objectName: "Contact"
   - fields: ["Name", "Account.Name", "Account.Owner.Name"]

4. Related object filtering:
   - objectName: "Contact"
   - fields: ["Name", "Account.Name"]
   - whereClause: "Account.Industry = 'Technology'"

Note: When using relationship fields:
- Use dot notation for parent relationships (e.g., "Account.Name")
- Use subqueries in parentheses for child relationships (e.g., "(SELECT Id FROM Contacts)")
- Custom relationship fields end in "__r" (e.g., "CustomObject__r.Name")
tools.salesforce_aggregate_query:
Execute SOQL queries with GROUP BY, aggregate functions, and statistical analysis. Use this tool for queries that summarize and group data rather than returning individual records.

NOTE: For regular queries without GROUP BY or aggregates, use salesforce_query_records instead.

This tool handles:
1. GROUP BY queries (single/multiple fields, related objects, date functions)
2. Aggregate functions: COUNT(), COUNT_DISTINCT(), SUM(), AVG(), MIN(), MAX()
3. HAVING clauses for filtering grouped results
4. Date/time grouping: CALENDAR_YEAR(), CALENDAR_MONTH(), CALENDAR_QUARTER(), FISCAL_YEAR(), FISCAL_QUARTER()

Examples:
1. Count opportunities by stage:
   - objectName: "Opportunity"
   - selectFields: ["StageName", "COUNT(Id) OpportunityCount"]
   - groupByFields: ["StageName"]

2. Analyze cases by priority and status:
   - objectName: "Case"
   - selectFields: ["Priority", "Status", "COUNT(Id) CaseCount", "AVG(Days_Open__c) AvgDaysOpen"]
   - groupByFields: ["Priority", "Status"]

3. Count contacts by account industry:
   - objectName: "Contact"
   - selectFields: ["Account.Industry", "COUNT(Id) ContactCount"]
   - groupByFields: ["Account.Industry"]

4. Quarterly opportunity analysis:
   - objectName: "Opportunity"
   - selectFields: ["CALENDAR_YEAR(CloseDate) Year", "CALENDAR_QUARTER(CloseDate) Quarter", "SUM(Amount) Revenue"]
   - groupByFields: ["CALENDAR_YEAR(CloseDate)", "CALENDAR_QUARTER(CloseDate)"]

5. Find accounts with more than 10 opportunities:
   - objectName: "Opportunity"
   - selectFields: ["Account.Name", "COUNT(Id) OpportunityCount"]
   - groupByFields: ["Account.Name"]
   - havingClause: "COUNT(Id) > 10"

Important Rules:
- All non-aggregate fields in selectFields MUST be included in groupByFields
- Use whereClause to filter rows BEFORE grouping
- Use havingClause to filter AFTER grouping (for aggregate conditions)
- ORDER BY can only use fields from groupByFields or aggregate functions
- OFFSET is not supported with GROUP BY in Salesforce
tools.salesforce_dml_records:
Perform data manipulation operations on Salesforce records:
  - insert: Create new records
  - update: Modify existing records (requires Id)
  - delete: Remove records (requires Id)
  - upsert: Insert or update based on external ID field
  Examples: Insert new Accounts, Update Case status, Delete old records, Upsert based on custom external ID
tools.salesforce_manage_object:
Create new custom objects or modify existing ones in Salesforce:
  - Create: New custom objects with fields, relationships, and settings
  - Update: Modify existing object settings, labels, sharing model
  Examples: Create Customer_Feedback__c object, Update object sharing settings
  Note: Changes affect metadata and require proper permissions
tools.salesforce_manage_field:
Create new custom fields or modify existing fields on any Salesforce object:
  - Field Types: Text, Number, Date, Lookup, Master-Detail, Picklist etc.
  - Properties: Required, Unique, External ID, Length, Scale etc.
  - Relationships: Create lookups and master-detail relationships
  - Automatically grants Field Level Security to System Administrator (or specified profiles)
  Examples: Add Rating__c picklist to Account, Create Account lookup on Custom Object
  Note: Use grantAccessTo parameter to specify profiles, defaults to System Administrator
tools.salesforce_manage_field_permissions:
Manage Field Level Security (Field Permissions) for custom and standard fields.
  - Grant or revoke read/edit access to fields for specific profiles or permission sets
  - View current field permissions
  - Bulk update permissions for multiple profiles
  
  Examples:
  1. Grant System Administrator access to a field
  2. Give read-only access to a field for specific profiles
  3. Check which profiles have access to a field
tools.salesforce_write_apex:
Create or update Apex classes in Salesforce.
  
Examples:
1. Create a new Apex class:
   {
     "operation": "create",
     "className": "AccountService",
     "apiVersion": "58.0",
     "body": "public class AccountService { public static void updateAccounts() { /* implementation */ } }"
   }

2. Update an existing Apex class:
   {
     "operation": "update",
     "className": "AccountService",
     "body": "public class AccountService { public static void updateAccounts() { /* updated implementation */ } }"
   }

Notes:
- The operation must be either 'create' or 'update'
- For 'create' operations, className and body are required
- For 'update' operations, className and body are required
- apiVersion is optional for 'create' (defaults to the latest version)
- The body must be valid Apex code
- The className in the body must match the className parameter
- Status information is returned after successful operations
tools.salesforce_write_apex_trigger:
Create or update Apex triggers in Salesforce.
  
Examples:
1. Create a new Apex trigger:
   {
     "operation": "create",
     "triggerName": "AccountTrigger",
     "objectName": "Account",
     "apiVersion": "58.0",
     "body": "trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert, before update) { /* implementation */ }"
   }

2. Update an existing Apex trigger:
   {
     "operation": "update",
     "triggerName": "AccountTrigger",
     "body": "trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert, before update, after update) { /* updated implementation */ }"
   }

Notes:
- The operation must be either 'create' or 'update'
- For 'create' operations, triggerName, objectName, and body are required
- For 'update' operations, triggerName and body are required
- apiVersion is optional for 'create' (defaults to the latest version)
- The body must be valid Apex trigger code
- The triggerName in the body must match the triggerName parameter
- The objectName in the body must match the objectName parameter (for 'create')
- Status information is returned after successful operations
tools.salesforce_execute_anonymous:
Execute anonymous Apex code in Salesforce.
  
Examples:
1. Execute simple Apex code:
   {
     "apexCode": "System.debug('Hello World');"
   }

2. Execute Apex code with variables:
   {
     "apexCode": "List<Account> accounts = [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 5]; for(Account a : accounts) { System.debug(a.Name); }"
   }

3. Execute Apex with debug logs:
   {
     "apexCode": "System.debug(LoggingLevel.INFO, 'Processing accounts...'); List<Account> accounts = [SELECT Id FROM Account LIMIT 10]; System.debug(LoggingLevel.INFO, 'Found ' + accounts.size() + ' accounts');",
     "logLevel": "DEBUG"
   }

Notes:
- The apexCode parameter is required and must contain valid Apex code
- The code is executed in an anonymous context and does not persist
- The logLevel parameter is optional (defaults to 'DEBUG')
- Execution results include compilation success/failure, execution success/failure, and debug logs
- For security reasons, some operations may be restricted based on user permissions
- This tool can be used for data operations or updates when there are no other specific tools available
- When users request data queries or updates that aren't directly supported by other tools, this tool can be used if the operation is achievable using Apex code
tools.salesforce_manage_debug_logs:
Manage debug logs for Salesforce users - enable, disable, or retrieve logs.
  
Examples:
1. Enable debug logs for a user:
   {
     "operation": "enable",
     "username": "user@example.com",
     "logLevel": "DEBUG",
     "expirationTime": 30
   }

2. Disable debug logs for a user:
   {
     "operation": "disable",
     "username": "user@example.com"
   }

3. Retrieve debug logs for a user:
   {
     "operation": "retrieve",
     "username": "user@example.com",
     "limit": 5
   }

4. Retrieve a specific log with full content:
   {
     "operation": "retrieve",
     "username": "user@example.com",
     "logId": "07L1g000000XXXXEAA0",
     "includeBody": true
   }

Notes:
- The operation must be one of: 'enable', 'disable', or 'retrieve'
- The username parameter is required for all operations
- For 'enable' operation, logLevel is optional (defaults to 'DEBUG')
- Log levels: NONE, ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, FINE, FINER, FINEST
- expirationTime is optional for 'enable' operation (minutes until expiration, defaults to 30)
- limit is optional for 'retrieve' operation (maximum number of logs to return, defaults to 10)
- logId is optional for 'retrieve' operation (to get a specific log)
- includeBody is optional for 'retrieve' operation (to include the full log content, defaults to false)
- The tool validates that the specified user exists before performing operations
- If logLevel is not specified when enabling logs, the tool will ask for clarification
